record_identity.title: Claude-assisted GTG-50029 campaign breached European political and media targets and exfiltrated sensitive data

incident_identity.historical_event_name: Anthropic GTG-50029 European political-target cyber campaign
incident_identity.date_basis: Anthropic describes the campaign as occurring in spring 2026 and publishes associated actor-infrastructure observations spanning 6 February through 4 July 2026. The range is an outer bound for evidenced campaign infrastructure, not a claim of continuous intrusion activity.

summary: Anthropic reported that a single French-speaking actor used Claude and an agentic multi-agent workflow to target European political parties, media organizations, think tanks and their SaaS providers. Across 42 tracked entities, the actor obtained internal access to at least 14, exfiltrated an estimated 12 to 26 GB of database dumps, and extracted approximately 140,000 records containing users' political opinions from one compromised political-campaign management platform. Other stolen material included donor and membership records, a 15,000-message mailbox, student application records including data from minors, payment-provider data, and credentials. Anthropic also reported per-victim encrypted archives staged on an actor-run Tor leak site.

vigil_assessment.factual_basis: Anthropic's September 2026 threat-intelligence report directly describes GTG-50029, including Claude-enabled agentic tooling, exploit development, at least 14 compromises among 42 tracked targets, approximately 140,000 political-opinion records from one campaign platform, and an estimated 12 to 26 GB of stolen data. Le Monde independently reported the same Anthropic-disclosed campaign and its concentration among French far-right organizations.
vigil_assessment.governance_interpretation: One actor used agentic coding, parallel sub-agents and AI-assisted exploit development to increase the speed, breadth and operational depth of a multi-target intrusion campaign. The public evidence establishes material offensive cyber uplift, but it does not isolate one reusable system failure or show that the model independently selected the malicious objective.
vigil_assessment.significance_to_cam: The campaign shows that frontier-model assistance can compress the labour and skill required for reconnaissance, exploit development, persistence, credential theft, data processing and multi-victim campaign management. Cyber governance therefore needs trajectory-level and cross-session controls rather than only local request filtering.
assessment_boundaries: Anthropic controls the underlying service telemetry; complete prompts, model traces, victim logs and exfiltrated datasets are not public.
The exact actor identity and complete victim list are not established in the reviewed public evidence.
Anthropic states that Claude Haiku, Sonnet and Opus were used across the cyber-operation cases in the report, but does not allocate every model version to every GTG-50029 action.
The record does not determine criminal or civil liability or notification status for each affected organization.
Malicious use and cyber uplift alone do not establish that the model or service violated a specific internal governance boundary.
